Name: Blue-Green Deployment
Strategy: Prepare and validate a replacement environment; promote by changing traffic routing; retain old capacity for recovery
Risk: Conditional - routing propagation and shared state can cause downtime or prevent rollback
Rollback Time: Routing convergence plus readiness or reprovisioning time; measure per environment
Blast Radius: Potentially all traffic at promotion; shared dependencies can affect both environments
Gotcha: Service selector changes are not globally atomic; delay old replica scale-down; verify router behavior and database compatibility before switching back

Name: Canary Deployment
Strategy: Expose a small initial cohort; increase traffic through measured steps with pauses and configured analysis
Risk: Conditional - analysis must be configured; small traffic exposure does not isolate shared state
Rollback Time: Detection and routing convergence plus stable capacity recovery; no fixed bound
Blast Radius: Configured traffic cohort initially; downstream effects may reach other users
Gotcha: Replica ratios only approximate traffic weights without a traffic router; match canary capacity to traffic and require adequate representative observations before promotion

Name: Rolling Update
Strategy: Replace replicas in batches using maxSurge and maxUnavailable; gate availability with readiness and minReadySeconds
Risk: Conditional - old and new versions coexist and require compatible APIs and data
Rollback Time: Another rollout of the retained Pod template; duration depends on readiness and capacity
Blast Radius: Grows with each batch; shared dependencies may broaden impact
Gotcha: ProgressDeadlineExceeded reports a stalled rollout but does not automatically undo it; retain revision history and explicitly orchestrate recovery

Name: Feature Flags
Strategy: Separate deployment from exposure using evaluated targeting rules; test both paths and plan temporary flag retirement
Risk: Conditional - cached or fallback values may differ across SDKs and disconnected clients
Rollback Time: Update propagation plus application reevaluation; disconnected clients have no fixed recovery bound
Blast Radius: Targeted contexts; shared writes or dependencies can affect other users
Gotcha: Disabling a flag does not undo side effects; distinguish off variation from code fallback; test update and outage behavior; check older clients and prerequisites before removing code or archiving flags

Name: Dark Launch
Strategy: Run sampled candidate reads alongside the control; compare results while returning the control response
Risk: Conditional - candidate work consumes resources and may delay or fail production requests
Rollback Time: Disable candidate execution; in-flight work and existing side effects remain
Blast Radius: Sampled requests plus shared dependencies; not zero user impact
Gotcha: Scientist is safe only for methods that do not change data; it does not protect against candidate timeouts; isolate writes and bound shadow load

Name: A/B Testing Release
Strategy: Assign experiment variants; evaluate business outcomes with guardrail metrics and assignment-quality checks
Risk: Conditional - controlled assignment does not ensure operational safety or valid inference
Rollback Time: Configuration propagation or redeployment; previous exposure cannot be undone
Gotcha: Check sample ratio mismatch and multiple exposures; use minimum data thresholds and a stopping rule appropriate to the statistical engine; sequential testing must be enabled when relied upon

Name: Recreate Deployment
Strategy: Terminate old Deployment Pods before creating new revision Pods during an upgrade
Risk: High availability risk for a service backed only by this Deployment
Rollback Time: Redeploy a compatible previous revision; includes termination and startup time
Blast Radius: All traffic served solely by the replaced Deployment
Gotcha: Recreate ordering applies to upgrades; manual Pod deletion may create a replacement while the old Pod terminates; it is not a general singleton or fencing guarantee

Name: GitOps
Strategy: Version desired state in Git; agents pull and reconcile it; recover by committing a compatible prior desired state
Risk: Conditional - reconciliation can fail and a Git revert does not restore external data
Rollback Time: Commit approval plus reconciliation and rollout time; no fixed bound
Blast Radius: Resources managed by the application and its deployment strategy
Tooling: Argo CD automated sync; OpenGitOps principles
Gotcha: Argo CD self-heal and pruning are opt-in; direct application rollback is unavailable with automated sync enabled; coordinate emergency edits with the controller and desired state

Name: Progressive Delivery
Strategy: Use staged exposure and configured analysis to promote or pause or abort; feature flags are optional
Risk: Conditional - automation enforces configured checks rather than guaranteeing a safe release
Rollback Time: Analysis interval and failure thresholds plus recovery convergence
Blast Radius: Expands with rollout steps; shared state can exceed the intended cohort
Tooling: Argo Rollouts AnalysisTemplate and AnalysisRun; Prometheus
Gotcha: Failed analysis can abort a rollout while inconclusive analysis pauses for intervention; dry-run metrics do not block promotion; aborting traffic does not reverse data changes

Name: Ring-Based Deployment
Strategy: Expose successive user or infrastructure cohorts; promote after health and usage checks over representative bake periods
Risk: Conditional - earlier rings may miss later-ring workloads and dependencies
Rollback Time: Stop subsequent rings first; recovery time depends on the underlying deployment
Blast Radius: Current and previously exposed rings; shared services may broaden impact
Tooling: Azure Pipelines stages and approval gates
Gotcha: Choose ring sizes and bake times for real usage patterns; no universal percentages; human approvals and emergency acceleration can complement automated gates

Name: Immutable Infrastructure
Strategy: Replace running resources from versioned configuration and artifacts instead of patching them in place
Risk: Conditional - recovery requires retained artifacts and compatible state plus replacement capacity
Rollback Time: Traffic switch or resource provisioning and health-check time
Blast Radius: Depends on replacement and traffic rollout strategy
Tooling: EC2 Image Builder; CloudFormation; versioned machine images
Gotcha: Immutability reduces drift but still requires detection and access controls; manage mutable data separately and do not assume previous images remain available forever

Name: Database Migration Safety
Strategy: Expand schema first; migrate and verify data; switch compatible readers and writers; contract only after old consumers and rollback dependencies are retired
Risk: High when destructive changes or long-running migrations affect shared state
Rollback Time: Application rollback only while data remains compatible; data recovery requires a measured repair or restore plan
Blast Radius: All applications sharing the schema or affected records
Tooling: Reviewed versioned migrations; Prisma Migrate; data verification queries
Gotcha: A one-time backfill may miss concurrent old-version writes; coordinate writes and reconciliation; test database-specific locking and transaction behavior; dropping old fields can make rollback unsafe

Name: Rollback Strategy
Strategy: Rehearse partial upgrade then full upgrade and downgrade under representative traffic; retain compatible artifacts and configuration; define recovery ownership
Risk: Conditional - prior code may no longer read data written by the new version
Rollback Time: Measure detection to restored service in drills; no strategy-independent time guarantee
Blast Radius: May exceed the original cohort through shared state or recovery actions
Tooling: Deployment runbooks; mixed-version tests; tested backup and restore procedures
Gotcha: Prepare all readers before activating new writers; activation can prevent rollback past the prepare version; code rollback does not undo data changes and down migrations need independent safety review

Name: Deployment Freeze
Strategy: Block routine production deployments during defined windows through deployment-job enforcement; define authorized emergency exceptions
Risk: Conditional - freezes reduce change exposure but do not prevent incidents or cover bypass paths
Rollback Time: N/A for the freeze itself; emergency recovery uses the normal recovery plan
Blast Radius: Environments and deployment paths covered by the gate
Tooling: GitLab deploy freeze windows and CI_DEPLOY_FREEZE job rules
Gotcha: A configured GitLab freeze sets a variable; deployment jobs must consume it to block execution; verify time zones and emergency procedures rather than relying on calendar entries

Name: Release Train
Strategy: Use a published release cadence with inclusion criteria and stabilization milestones; defer unready work and review exceptions
Risk: Conditional - predictable dates do not make a large batch low risk
Rollback Time: Depends on artifact compatibility and deployment mechanism; not the release cadence
Blast Radius: Changes included in the train and the population reached by its rollout
Tooling: Release milestones; CI; release branches; approved cherry-picks
Gotcha: Do not waive readiness checks to meet a date; maintain an approved urgent-fix path and staged deployment; a release train does not require simultaneous exposure of all features

Name: Canary Analysis Gates
Strategy: Compare version-specific canary and concurrent control signals plus absolute SLO limits; require representative traffic and observation windows
Risk: Conditional - sparse samples or shared failures can hide regressions
Rollback Time: Detection window plus configured abort and recovery time
Blast Radius: Canary cohort initially; shared failures may affect control too
Tooling: Argo Rollouts AnalysisTemplates; Prometheus; version-labelled SLIs
Gotcha: Define explicit handling for empty results and NaN and provider errors; do not promote on missing evidence; background analysis ending successfully is not proof of sufficient observations

Name: Graceful Shutdown and Connection Draining
Strategy: Gate new replicas with readiness; stop accepting new work and drain in-flight connections during termination
Risk: Conditional - propagation races and work exceeding the grace period can cause errors
Rollback Time: Recovery requires healthy replacement capacity; terminated requests are not restored
Blast Radius: Affected connections and requests on terminating replicas
Gotcha: preStop consumes the termination grace budget; remaining processes can be force-killed when it expires; test load-balancer draining and long-lived connections under rollout load

Name: Digest-Pinned Artifact Promotion
Strategy: Promote the tested container image by digest across environments; track compatible configuration and retain recovery artifacts
Risk: Conditional - digest identifies content but does not prove trust or application compatibility
Rollback Time: Pull and rollout time for a retained compatible image; registry access may delay recovery
Tooling: Kubernetes image digests; container registry retention; versioned release configuration
Gotcha: Tags can be moved and imagePullPolicy Always does not pin content; digest pinning does not preserve deleted artifacts or freeze external configuration and data
